The restaurant still has a feel from those days including paintings from the era on the walls, and some dishes are named after the famous patrons from those days.

voyage.name: Kaffecentralen
voyage.content: This little shop concentrates on selling espresso paraphernalia, and also serves excellent cappuccino.

voyage.name: Café and Eepos
voyage.content: A hidden gem. Delicious pastries, pies and buns – and books for reading. There are even glasses available for those with poor eyesight.

voyage.name: Café Regatta
voyage.content: A pleasant little café located at the seashore in western Töölö. Serves good coffee and pastries. In summertime, the café tends to be absolutely packed with locals and tourists. You're better off sitting at the terrace rather than inside the café. Coffee costs 2 EUR, but if you have an additional cup, the café actually gives you 5 cents back instead of charging you.

voyage.name: Sinisen huvilan kahvila
voyage.content: The "Café of the Blue Villa" is an outdoors café with fantastic views over the Töölönlahti bay.

voyage.name: Café Tin Tin Tango
voyage.content: A uniquely Helsinki combination of café, restaurant, bar, laundromat and sauna, Tin Tin Tango serves up all-day breakfast, soups, salads and sandwiches, but stays open late with wine and occasional live music. Laundry/dryer €4/2. Sauna rental €22-32/hour (1–10 people), reservations required.

voyage.name: Korjaamo
voyage.hours: Café open daily 11:00–17:00, bar Mon Tue 16:00–11:00, Wed Thu 16:00-01:00, Fri Sat 16:00–03:00, Sun closed
voyage.content: Nice terrace, two floor laid back bar with live DJs in the evening and café in the building of the Korjaamo Cultural Factory. Free access to Apple computers with Internet, Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Olutravintola Vastarannan Kiiski
voyage.content: Beer from all over the world.

voyage.name: Storyville
voyage.content: Jazz club and restaurant, often live music.

voyage.name: St. Urho's Pub
voyage.content: A nice, cosy traditional pub. Quite spacious interior. Over a hundred beers and ciders available, on tap and in bottles. The food is a bit pricey.

voyage.name: Summer Hostel Academica
voyage.content: Summer hostel.

voyage.name: Helka
voyage.content: A dependable old standby.

voyage.name: Scandic Park Helsinki
voyage.content: A large, modern hotel catering to families, leisure travellers, and business travellers. Over 500 rooms, sauna, exercise facilities, Wi-Fi, restaurant and bar. Breakfast included.

voyage.name: Hellsten Helsinki Parliament
voyage.content: A modern hotel in an old apartment building. Rooms are modern, spacious and have nice views to the park across the street and to the others architecturally beautiful buildings.

voyage.name: Crowne Plaza
voyage.content: Modern furniture. Gym with a pool.

voyage.name: Alppipuisto
voyage.content: Located on the west side of the Linnanmäki amusement park, this beautiful park is a hidden gem during the summer due to the many free concerts and other events that are held there throughout the summer months.

voyage.name: Bear park
voyage.content: A cosy small park on the hill next to Kallio church and one of Kallio's symbols. The park got its name from the bear statue in the middle of it.

voyage.name: Church of Kallio
voyage.content: On top of the hill at the end of Siltasaarenkatu. The church is built of grey granite (1912) and its massive looks dominate the view from Hakaniemi. It was designed by Finnish architect Lars Sonck. The church has both baroque and French romantic organs and concerts are organized frequently. The bells ring at noon and 19:00 with a tune composed by Jean Sibelius.

voyage.name: Church of St. Paul
voyage.content: A church from the 1930s built of red tiles, one of the first landmarks one will see when driving into Helsinki from Lahti.

voyage.name: Graffiti
voyage.content: The Pasila neighbourhood is known for its large collection of graffiti, making it a popular destination for street art enthusiasts.

voyage.name: Suvilahti
voyage.content: A cultural centre in a former power plant and gasworks area, which has become home to a wide range of cultural actors.. Features a 100-metre-long wall where graffiti is legally permitted and the artwork is constantly evolving.

voyage.name: Technology museum
voyage.content: A small museum dedicated to technology, machines and industry.

voyage.name: Tropicario
voyage.content: Watch some of those tropical animals you wouldn't want to bite or sting you in the indoor terrarium Tropicario.

voyage.name: Vanhakaupunki and Vanhakaupunki rapids
voyage.content: The place where Vantaa river flows into the sea was the place where Helsinki was founded in 1550. Despite its name "Old Town", don't expect to find any medieval buildings there, as the area was devastated by a fire and a plague outbreak and subsequently the city was moved south to its current location. Nevertheless, the site of where Helsinki was founded is marked by a small memorial and nearby there's the site of th

voyage.name: Worker Housing Museum
voyage.content: Built for the city's employees and their families in the early 20th century, nowadays the house is a museum where every room is a snapshot of the inhabitants' everyday life during different decades from the 1920s to the 1980s. Visits by guided tours which are free, start about every 15-20 minutes depending on how many visitors have arrived, and are conducted in Finnish, English (whenever foreign travellers show up) a

voyage.name: Kalasatama
voyage.content: Literally "fish harbour", this is a new seafront neighbourhood which has an interesting brick touch to it. Not a typical tourist destination, but some architecture lovers might find the place interesting. Also home to a big, crazy statue of a Siberian Jay. A new shopping and living complex Redi has been built there, with the first phase opened in autumn 2018.

voyage.name: Majakka
voyage.content: Literally "lighthouse", the Majakka tower is 134 metres (440 ft) tall high-rise building, known as the first skyscraper of Finland. It was inaugurated in 2019.

voyage.name: Torkkelinmäki
voyage.content: The green parks and small apartment buildings on the top of a hill and in the centre of Finland's densest-populated neighbourhood are protected as an exemplary early-20th century working-class cultural environment. Around, you will find a former university at Franzéninkatu 13 and a former technical school at Agricolankatu 1-3, as well as small cafes, bars and restaurants.

voyage.name: Helsinki Fair Grounds
voyage.content: For many business travellers the reason to visit Helsinki, but there are also some events around the year that aren't exclusively geared towards professionals like the American car show in April, the book fair in October, ski expo in November and the travel expo in January.

voyage.name: Kallio Kukkii
voyage.content: A cultural summer festival held in the bohemian district of Kallio not very far from the city centre. Held over a week in middle May. Various art galleries, workshops and street art performances. Culminates in a samba parade on Sunday, held by Império do Papagaio as their final practice before the main Samba Carnaval in the city centre.

voyage.name: Kulttuuritalo
voyage.content: The Helsinki Hall of Culture is a concert hall designed by Alvar Aalto in the 1950s, and part of the Aalto Works . Since its opening, many world-famous artists and groups such as Jimi Hendrix, AC/DC, Tina Turner, Iron Maiden and Lady Gaga have held concerts there.

voyage.name: Linnanmäki
voyage.content: The oldest amusement park in Finland, famous for its wooden roller coaster. Entrance to the park is free of charge, all-day passes €42. Open only during the summer, however the adjacent Sea Life aquarium and the Peacock theatre (not a traditional theatre but rather a venue for musicals and slightly Las Vegas-like shows) at Tivolikuja 1 is open throughout the year.In middle October, the amusement park holds a week-lon

voyage.name: Suvilahti
voyage.content: A former power plant, nowadays a centre for alternative culture that hosts a circus and some exhibitions. The famous metal festival Tuska at the turn of June and July and electronic music festival Flow in August are held on the premises.

voyage.name: Suvilahti DIY
voyage.content: A popular skatepark built by the skaters themselves. The place has even been used by many internationally famous skaters, such as Tony Hawk. It has been under threat since 2017, losing an appeal in 2024.

voyage.name: Tokoinranta
voyage.content: A park north-west of Hakaniemi, which in August turns into an outdoor scene during the Helsingin Juhlaviikot cultural festival. Check out the City theatre, and if you understand Finnish or Swedish, go see a theatre performance.

voyage.name: Brahenkenttä
voyage.content: An open sports pitch in northern Kallio where you can play football (soccer) in the summer and ice hockey or bandy in the winter or watch a home game of the Finnish bandy league team HIFK.

voyage.name: Mäkelänrinne swimming hall
voyage.content: Indoor swimming pool which has also been used for international competitions. Great if you feel like swimming in the winter but don't care for the traditional Finnish "hole in the ice" swimming.

voyage.name: Urheilutalo
voyage.content: The "Sports house" offers swimming, bowling or exercising.

voyage.name: Arlan sauna
voyage.content: Old public sauna in Kallio. Separate saunas for men and women. Washing service and traditional bloodletting (kuppaus) also available.

voyage.name: Kotiharjun sauna
voyage.price: €12 for adults, students & pensioners €8.5, towel €3 extra.
voyage.content: This is the last wood-burning public sauna in Helsinki. Separate saunas for men and women. There's a good chance you'll find a top level chess match in the dressing room. Don't miss cooling off outside, especially in winter. On Saturdays you'll find bachelor parties (Kotiharju is pretty near to Kallio's nightlife).

voyage.name: Sauna Vogue
voyage.content: Only gay sauna in Finland.

voyage.name: Arabia Factory Shop
voyage.content: Factory outlet for Arabia ceramics and Iittala glassware, best known for selling slightly defective goods at modestly discounted prices.

voyage.name: Vallilan Akseli
voyage.content: Here you can watch and buy "design"-furniture and kitchen utilities.

voyage.name: Moko market and café
voyage.content: Things to furnish and decorate your home of the more expensive kind as well as organic products. They have a café too, serving sandwiches, good hamburgers and a range of beverages – on Saturdays you can enjoy brunch there. Moko has another branch in Punavuori in the southwest of the city.

voyage.name: Kauppakeskus Arabia
voyage.content: A shopping mall in northwestern Helsinki with two supermarkets and some speciality stores.

voyage.name: REDI
voyage.content: Shopping mall opened in September 2018, built around the Kalasatama metro station. Redi is said to be the most labyrinthine shopping centre in Europe, mostly because the metro tracks cuts the mall in half, so that is by itself an interesting thing to experience. The Majakka building on top of the mall is the second tallest skyscraper in the Nordic countries (after Turning Torso in Malmö).

voyage.name: Hakaniemi Market Hall and Open-Air Market
voyage.content: A busy indoor market hall and outdoor market square frequented by locals, this is where you can find fresh produce and specialities or have a cup of coffee or a small meal. The open-air market offers fresh vegetables and seasonal products, and a flea market on the first Sunday each month at which point there will be a much greater number of food and goods vendors from all over Finland. Walking up Hämeentie from Hakan

voyage.name: Black & White
voyage.content: Rock. Many genres. Very recommended.

voyage.name: Hippie Shake records
voyage.content: Rare 1960/70s rock and hard rock.

voyage.name: Goofin Records
voyage.content: Rockabilly.

voyage.name: Dos Tecolotes
voyage.content: Dos Tecolotes (Spanish for "two eagle-owls") sells Mexican foods and foodstuffs that the owners import directly from Mexico.

voyage.name: Helsingin Pantti
voyage.content: A pawn shop.

voyage.name: Poromagia
voyage.content: A full-service board, card and miniature game store.

voyage.name: Student's restaurant at Arcada
voyage.hours: Food around lunchtime, coffee, sandwich and cakes all day
voyage.content: Like most other university campuses, the Swedish-language polytechnic Arcada has a lunch restaurant operated by Amica. Even if you aren't a student, the prices for lunch are quite cheap.

voyage.name: Blinit
voyage.content: Another Russian eatery specialized in blini with different fillings. Also pelmeny and soups (borscht specially recommended) on daily offer.

voyage.name: Pelmenit
voyage.content: Serves pelmeny (Russian dumplings), blini (Russian crepes), soups and salads. The menu depends on the mood of the Russian owner.

voyage.name: Almas
voyage.content: A Persian restaurant.

voyage.name: Bites Burgers
voyage.content: Tasty burgers made to order, with a regular, vegan, vegetarian and special option that can be further customised. They have a good selection of sodas and craft beer. They also have restaurants in Kamppi and the Kaivopiha mall.

voyage.name: Bunthan's Food
voyage.content: A Thai restaurant.

voyage.name: Cella
voyage.content: Established 1969, this is one of the oldest restaurants in the Kallio district, serving classic Finnish food with lots of grease and salt. For a "real" restaurant (not fast food) in Helsinki it's reasonably priced, around €10-20 for main dishes. The chef himself often serves the food, complete with a sexist joke or an insult, and may even force feed you the leftovers if you don't finish your meal! Also serves as a pu

voyage.name: Freeesh
voyage.price: Lunch buffet €13.90, evening and weekend buffet €16.90
voyage.content: A sushi buffet restaurant in the Kalasatama neighbourhood. The sushi is fresh and tasty. The restaurant is very popular and a bit small, so prepare for queues. Soft drinks included in the price but alcoholic drinks cost extra.

voyage.name: Grand Georgia
voyage.content: Wäiski is the only year-round restaurant boat in Helsinki. You cannot travel anywhere with it, as it is firmly docked at Hakaniemi Pier. Both indoor and outdoor seating and fair prices. However the boat is sometimes rented for private parties and conferences and in that case you need to go elsewhere. A Georgian restaurant since 2018.

voyage.name: Bar Loosister
voyage.content: Good selection of burgers and beers on tap. Chicken wings with four different sauces, the hottest one "hot as fuck" is absolutely scorching hot.

voyage.name: Musta Härkä
voyage.content: Decent restaurant in Vallila serving Indian and Western food, although most people just drop in to have a beer or two. Karaoke and sometimes live music.

voyage.name: Oiva
voyage.content: A famous restaurant in the bohemian district of Kallio, dating back to 1940. Featured in Helsinkian folklore. A wide variety of à la carte dishes and affordable lunch on weekdays.

voyage.name: Old Sophie
voyage.content: Casual neighbourhood restaurant. Ordinary Finnish food, meat and pasta dishes, pizzas, burgers, Indian food, desserts. Own menu for children, toys available.

voyage.name: Onda
voyage.content: Mediterranean-style restaurant in Kallio. Specialises in vegetarian food but has meat and fish dishes too. The inside of the restaurant is a bit cramped but there is a spacious terrace. Lunch buffet on weekdays, à la carte dishes on evenings and Saturdays. Note that the "XXX hot" chili sauce at the buffet really is hot.

voyage.name: Pastelaria Brazil
voyage.content: A Brazilian restaurant.

voyage.name: Pronto Pizzeria
voyage.content: A nice pizzeria on the street Hämeentie. Serves a wide variety of pizzas and salads. Stylish Italian decor. Not to be confused with restaurant Pronto at the Helsinki Central railway station.

voyage.name: Silvoplee
voyage.content: Vegetarian restaurant specialising in living and raw foods but also serves warm dishes. Buffet, pay per weight. Closed on Sunday.

voyage.name: Weeruska
voyage.content: Serves simple, but tasty, home-made style food. The clientele at lunch is primarily blue-collar workers and the portions are sized accordingly.

voyage.name: Taverna Zorbas
voyage.content: Kallio's favourite Greek restaurant.

voyage.name: Kahvila Sävy
voyage.content: Small, retro style café with excellent coffee from a Finnish roastery. There are only a few seats in the former barbershop, next to the Sörnäinen metro. Also peculiar percolators for sale.

voyage.name: Kipsari
voyage.content: Student cafe at the University of Art and Industrial Design in Arabia. Relaxed atmosphere with live music and DJs at times. Not open during summer when the school's out.

voyage.name: Juttutupa
voyage.content: Helsinki's (probably) oldest still operational pub, housed in the "workers' house", a nice old granite house called Graniittilinna. It has historically been the bar of the political left. While Lenin was hiding out in Finland planning the upcoming Russian revolution he was known to frequent Juttutupa; the table he used to sit at is kept in his memory (the one in the back with a good view of the entrance). On Wednesda

voyage.name: Lepakkomies
voyage.price: Free entry to bar, but entrance fee for club nights. Beer starting from €4
voyage.content: The name translates to "bat-man" but the place is hardly themed after Batman, instead after bats in general. A large establishment in two floors, the ground floor functioning as your average Kallio pub, the basement as a venue for club nights.

voyage.name: Mascot
voyage.content: A large and comfortable pub in Kallio. Rough-edge decor typical of Kallio. Regularly hosts live music performances and other events.

voyage.name: Bar Molotow
voyage.content: Small and always cosy indie/alternative/electro/goth rock bar. Nice summer terrace.

voyage.name: Musta kissa
voyage.content: The name translates to "black cat". A popular bar among young and beautiful expats and their Finnish friends. Often nights with alternative DJs, awesome live music, performances and experimental art.

voyage.name: Pub Fairytale
voyage.content: A small but cosy gay bar. It has daily happy hour and free internet access available, with regular events like karaoke nights and bear art exhibitions.

voyage.name: Roskapankki
voyage.content: A Kallio institution. The name stems from the 1990s depression: just invest your money in beer, instead of depositing them at a bank going bankrupt. Live music some nights.

voyage.name: Siltanen
voyage.content: A popular hipster haunt from the owners of the next door Kuudes Linja club venue (see below). Part bar, part club and part café (with food served until 22:00) with a big terrace and weird décor and DJs and the occasional live gig in the evenings. Weekend DJ brunch 12:00-16:00, prepare to wait for a table though.

voyage.name: Toveri
voyage.content: Small bar with various types of beer. It's been here in various forms since 1937, and is one of the prettiest bars in Kallio.

voyage.name: Kuudes linja
voyage.content: A live music oriented nightclub for the somewhat artsy crowd. Located in the Kallio district Kuudes linja usually offers more experimental and alternative music than the mainstream downtown clubs and also hosts electronic music parties. Arrive early to avoid queues on popular nights — admittance is not guaranteed once the place gets full. The weatherproof terrace in the courtyard is open during the summer – you

voyage.name: Leblon Merihaka
voyage.hours: May-Sep lunchtime to late if it's not raining
voyage.content: A kind of outdoor food court/bar, right at the seafront comprising a set of kiosks serving fast food (hamburgers, Middle Eastern among others), ice cream, beer and wine with a seating area in the middle. Live music many nights, often featuring names of Helsinki's hip hop and DJ scene, and there are often also other events in Leblon like yoga in the morning. Doesn't really have regular opening times, if the weather is

voyage.name: Super Bario
voyage.content: A video game bar.

voyage.name: AVA Hotelli
voyage.price: From €49 in the low season, also monthly rates
voyage.content: Affordable hotel in Kumpula, popular among Russian visitors.

voyage.name: CheapSleep Helsinki
voyage.content: Opened in May 2012.

voyage.name: Citybox Helsinki
voyage.content: Opened in February 2024.

voyage.name: Cumulus Hakaniemi
voyage.price: From €83 for a double in the low season
voyage.content: A centrally located business hotel.

voyage.name: Cumulus Olympia
voyage.price: From €83 for a double in the low season
voyage.content: A business hotel near the city centre.

voyage.name: Korkeasaari
voyage.hours: Every day except Christmas Eve: 10:00-20:00, may operate shorter hours on holidays
voyage.content: Helsinki's zoo, with approximately 150 different animal species. The zoos signature animals are the bears, the free-roaming peafowls and the cats (from tigers and lions to European wildcats). Another highlight is Amazonia, a partly underground house featuring tropical plants and smaller animals such as fish and frogs. Opened in 1889, Korkeasaari is reportedly one of the world's oldest operating zoos. Korkeasaari is c

voyage.name: Kultturikeskus STOA
voyage.content: One of Helsinki's modern cultural centers hosting various galleries.

voyage.name: Roihuvuori Cherry Park and Japanese garden
voyage.content: Two adjacent Japanese-style parks in Roihuvuori. The best time to visit is in the spring during the cherry blossom when a traditional Japanese hanami is celebrated.

voyage.name: Vartiokylä fortress hill
voyage.content: Ruins of a medieval fortification.

voyage.name: Tammisalo Canal
voyage.content: The canal was dug in 1762 by the owner of the Herttoniemi manor to provide a shortcut for fishermen from Porvoo to the Helsinki Market Square. Before that it was a natural strait, through which Russian warships attacked Helsinki during the Greater Wrath. It was filled in 1794, but was re-opened as a local sight in 2001.

voyage.name: Cirrus
voyage.content: At 86 m, Cirrus was the tallest building in Finland when opened; with Majakka finished, it's not even the tallest in Helsinki, but still a notable landmark in Vuosaari. There were plans to make the an observation platform of the highest floor, which weren't realized.

voyage.name: Östersundom Church
voyage.content: A wooden church from 1754.

voyage.name: Helsinki Heart Stone
voyage.content: This stone lies at the geographical centre of Helsinki. After using public transport, you will have to continue your journey on foot, as it is in the middle of a forest.

voyage.name: Aurinkolahti Beach
voyage.content: Spacier and calmer than Hietsu in Western Helsinki, the Aurinkolahti Beach is frequented by everyone from youth to families.

voyage.name: Hoplop activity hall for kids
voyage.content: 8-meter-tall adventure maze, slides, cafe.

voyage.name: Natura Viva - Vuosaari Paddling Center
voyage.content: Kayak rental open from the beginning of June until the end of August every day. In May and September on demand. Guided tours, trips and courses are also possible.

voyage.name: Uutela Nature Trail
voyage.content: A nature trail, about 4 km long in eastern Helsinki.

voyage.name: Vuosaarenhuippu Hill Hiking Trails
voyage.content: Plenty of routes for hikers of all levels, from easy-to-walk service roads to rocky little paths.

voyage.name: Kontufestari
voyage.content: Yearly music festival in Kontula with performances by Finnish 1980s rock artists and hip hop crews from Eastern Helsinki among others.

voyage.name: Metro
voyage.content: A little known fact is that Helsinki Metro is the world's northernmost metro system. Why not ride all the way to Mellunmäki, which is the world's northernmost metro station?

voyage.name: Mustavuori forest and Östersundom bird waters
voyage.content: The area is protected under the European Union's Natura 2000 ecological network program. There are many different forest types and bird species here.

voyage.name: Ramsinniemi protected area
voyage.content: A small nature reserve.

voyage.name: Skata Pks4H Petting Zoo
voyage.content: In Skata you will find several different domestic animals such as sheep. Children can hug animals.

voyage.name: Itis
voyage.content: One of the largest shopping malls in the Nordic countries with some 240 shops. If that's not enough, there is a separate Prisma hypermarket right across Kehä I, a Citymarket across Itäväylä and the "grandfather" Puhos (opened in 1965) behind Itis itself, all with small stores. Comes with an unexpected African and Middle Eastern vibe due to the high number of immigrants residing in the nearby neighbourhoods, who spend

voyage.name: Hertsi
voyage.content: Herttoniemi district's shopping centre.

voyage.name: Saari
voyage.content: A shopping centre including about 20 stores.

voyage.name: Columbus
voyage.content: If you're in the easternmost part and need to buy something, check out Vuosaari's Columbus, with some 50 stores.

voyage.name: Marimekko Factory Outlet
voyage.content: Fans of likely the best known Finnish fashion and interior design brand will find this a reason to venture out into the East of Helsinki.

voyage.name: Karhusaaren kauppa Winberg & Winberg
voyage.content: A shop offering daily goods, with a cafe in connection with it, which welcomes islanders and vacationers arriving by land and by boat. In the summer, the merchant ship Christina offers all groceries, food, drinks, gases, soils and, if necessary, also custom products, such as small quantities of building materials.

voyage.name: Kontula shopping centre
voyage.content: A local shopping center with stores and restaurants near the metro station.

voyage.name: Alanya Market
voyage.content: A grocery store specializing in Middle Eastern products.

voyage.name: Eestin Herkut
voyage.content: A little bit of Estonia in Helsinki. A rather small grocery store selling Estonian food and drink products not available at Finnish supermarkets, as well as Estonian-language magazines. There is even Estonian music playing in the background. Note that the store does not sell any alcohol.

voyage.name: Streetbeat
voyage.content: One of Finland's dance/electronic music pioneers, but they've closed their city center store and moved into the suburbs.

voyage.name: Hungry Hub Vuosaari
voyage.content: A fast food restaurant.

voyage.name: King Kebab Herttoniemi
voyage.content: A fast food restaurant.

voyage.name: Royal Namaskaar
voyage.content: An Indian restaurant.

voyage.name: Southland
voyage.content: Quite standard Westernized Chinese fare, but unbeatable value for money in Helsinki, as most dishes only set you back €7-8, even during dinner time.

voyage.name: Tikke
voyage.content: Chosen as one of the best kebab restaurants in Helsinki by many locals. Especially the shish kebab is worth trying.

voyage.name: Waste&Feast Snellu Cafe
voyage.content: Prepares meals from store surplus dishes.

voyage.name: Fornitaly
voyage.content: A pizzeria.

voyage.name: Ravintola Fregatti
voyage.hours: Mon-Thu 10:00–23:00, Fri Sat 10:00–00:00, Sun 11:00–22:00; buffet lunch Mon–Sat

voyage.name: Ravintola Gurkha
voyage.content: Nepalese restaurant.

voyage.name: Martisor Ravintola
voyage.content: A Somalian restaurant.

voyage.name: Mandraki
voyage.content: A Greek restaurant.

voyage.name: Suola & Pippuri
voyage.content: Offering unpretentious Finnish fare, probably one of the best options inside shopping centre Itis if you're hungry.

voyage.name: Thai Orchid Itis
voyage.content: Offers an excellent and authentic Thai buffet (including decent sushi) during lunchtime inside shopping centre Itis.

voyage.name: Wanha Mylly
voyage.address: Linnanrakentajantie 12 but Johan Sederholmintie 8 (behind the building) if you need to park your car
voyage.content: Casual fine dining in the former Herttoniemi manor. Specializes in steaks, with the large Lankkupihvi steak served on a wooden platter as the house special. Extensive wine list which you wouldn't expect to find in this part of Helsinki. In the summer you can enjoy your meal in the outdoor garden if you like.

voyage.name: Kulosaaren Casino
voyage.content: Hosted in the old casino on Kulosaari, this restaurant is your second alternative if you want to have a finer meal. Popular among diplomats, as many embassies are located on Kulosaari island.

voyage.name: Pikkulintu
voyage.content: An unassuming pub in an assuming location, but offers an excellent selection of beer and whiskey (to see what's on tap, check the website). Offers occasionally beer and whiskey tastings as well.

voyage.name: Solmu
voyage.content: Spacious and stylish pub with a good selection of beers and ciders. Often hosts entertainment nights with pub quizzes, live music or stand-up comedy.

voyage.name: Svenkka
voyage.content: Located on the grounds of Puotila Manor, has a nice terrace to enjoy a pint on a warm summer's day.

voyage.name: Rastila Camping
voyage.content: The only camping site inside Helsinki borders. Seventeen minute metro ride from the Central Railway Station.

voyage.name: Conference Hotel Sofia
voyage.content: A conference hotel in Vuosaari. It also hosts a gallery of Orthodox Christian art and offers yoga lessons.

voyage.name: Hotel Jollas89
voyage.content: Hotel which is located on green and calm surroundings with easy public transport access to city centre.

voyage.name: Conference Hotel Rantapuisto
voyage.price: weekday rates from €119, weekend rates from €73
voyage.content: Conference hotel not far from Rastila Camping of the chain Finlandia Hotels.

voyage.name: Malmi airport
voyage.content: Located north of Malmi, the airport was the general aviation airport of Helsinki after the opening of Helsinki Airport. After two decades of planning, debates and protests, the airport was shut down entirely in 2021 after functioning as an uncontrolled airfield for a few years. The City of Helsinki will turn the area into a new residential district, though the functionalist terminal building will be preserved.

voyage.name: Tuomarinkylä Manor Museum
voyage.content: A look into the daily life on an 18th-century manor. Also hosts a restaurant and a riding school.

voyage.name: Rhododendron park
voyage.content: Helsinki University's rhododendron research garden in the Haaga district is also a public park that you can visit around the year. Best time to for visiting are in early or mid-June when the rhododendrons bloom.

voyage.name: Kannelmäki Church
voyage.content: Finished in 1968 and looking like a copper pyramid with windows along the edges forming a cross. It's listed by the Finnish National Board of Antiquities as a "nationally remarkable built cultural environment".

voyage.name: Tapanila Church
voyage.content: The 1957 church building designed by Per Björkvall, which is the oldest church in the entire Malmi parish.

voyage.name: Malmi Cemetery
voyage.content: The biggest cemetery in the country by number of burials. Many Finnish cultural and political personalities are buried here. Other things worth seeing are the main chapel built in 1923 which is still used, as well as the cemetery's own water tower and railway station, both of which are disused.

voyage.name: Pet Cemetery
voyage.content: An animal cemetery established in 1947 and maintained by HESY ry, the animal protection association of Helsinki, contains about 3,000 graves.

voyage.name: Malmi Krishna Temple
voyage.content: An ISKCON temple.

voyage.name: Bodybuilding Club
voyage.content: A gym founded in 1968. It has been visited by bodybuilding legends Arnold Schwarzenegger, Franco Columbo and Frank Zane, among others.

voyage.name: Fallkulla Farm
voyage.content: In Fallkulla you can get to know the traditional farm animals: sheep, goats, cattle, ducks, chickens, rabbits and horses.

voyage.name: Haltiala Farm
voyage.content: A kind of a zoo with farm animals in a real countryside environment. The Haltiala farm has many domestic animals such as cows, sheep, pigs and chickens. They are outdoors from summer to autumn, allowing them to be seen in the courtyard from morning to night. For the rest of the year, the animals are indoors. Occasionally country music concerts are held at Haltiala.

voyage.name: Helsinki Central Park
voyage.content: This is a huge park starting just north of the Olympic Stadium and extending northwards for 10 km. It encompasses an area of over 1,000 hectares. The park is mostly in a natural state, with plenty of walkways, bikeways, riding paths and sports facilities including Pirkkola Sports Park (ice hockey, swimming, running) and Paloheinä (skiing, golf). A popular jogging area.

voyage.name: Kanneltalo
voyage.content: A concert and exhibition hall in Kannelmäki.

voyage.name: Malminkartanonhuippu
voyage.content: With a height of about 90 m, this is the highest point in Helsinki and when you've climbed the 426 stairs to the top you're rewarded with a nice view in all directions. In winter this is a great place for sledding. The hill itself is actually an old landfill and consists mostly of building material which has given the hill nicknames such as the dump hill or filling hill! Can be accessed from two directions, either fr

voyage.name: Malminkartano Apple Garden
voyage.content: There are 350 trees in Malminkartano garden. Most are apple trees, but there are also pear, plum and cherry trees. Guests are free to pick fruit from the trees.

voyage.name: Malmitalo
voyage.content: A culture centre.

voyage.name: Power&Go Fallkulla
voyage.content: A gym.

voyage.name: Sugoi
voyage.content: An arcade game hall in the Malmi district. Minimum age 12.

voyage.name: Tapanilan Erän Karate
voyage.content: A sports club focused on karate.

voyage.name: Beer Floating
voyage.content: An unofficial event usually held the last weekend of July or the first weekend of August since 1997. The participants (yup, mostly males in their 20s) gather in Vantaa with rubber boats, rafts or whatever they can find that floats and travel downstream towards the Vanhankaupunki rapids while indulging beer – of course without life vests. This event has no official arrangers that could be held responsible if something

voyage.name: Kaari
voyage.content: Prisma hypermarket and about 80 other businesses.

voyage.name: Ristikko
voyage.content: Also features an indoor climbing area.

voyage.name: Malmin Nova
voyage.content: The southeastern half of the shopping complex on both sides of the railway in Malmi. Connected to Malmintori with a covered walking bridge through the Malmi railway station.

voyage.name: Malmintori
voyage.content: The northwestern half of the shopping complex on both sides of the railway in Malmi. Connected to Malmin Nova with a covered walking bridge through the Malmi railway station.

voyage.name: Varusteleka
voyage.content: A bit outside the centre but reachable by public transport, is Europe's biggest military surplus store. Has probably the friendliest and the most knowledgeable staff you'll find in Finland. Varusteleka sells anything from modern combat gear, to 1930s Nazi leather trench coats, to very good value-for-money modern gore-tex hiking coats that some army somewhere had too many of.

voyage.name: Sopilka
voyage.content: Ukrainian grocery store.

voyage.name: Moi Market
voyage.content: A grocery store selling Asian and Middle Eastern foods.

voyage.name: Marian Konditoria
voyage.content: Sandwiches, pastries and cakes fresh out of the oven at the bakery's café.

voyage.name: Ravintola Rumpu
